newsitem.title: RWANDA: Twenty-one people, most children, killed in Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: Twenty-one people, most children, killed in Rwanda.

text.p: Unidentified gunmen in eastern Rwanda killed 21 people, most of them children, who returned late last year from Tanzania, the victims' neighbours said on Saturday.

The neighbours, who declined to be identified, said they heard screams and gunshots at about midnight on Thursday and in the morning found 11 people dead at one house and 10 dead at another 150 metres (yards) away.
The 21 people -- five adults and 16 children -- had been shot dead. They were all Hutus, the majority ethnic group.
"We have no idea who could have done this. Nobody here saw anything," said a farmer who lived close to one of the houses.
Killings have increased in Rwanda since the return of more than a million Hutu refugees from Tanzania and Zaire in the last two months of last year.
The refugees fled in 1994, fearing reprisals for the genocide of 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus by Hutu troops, militiamen and mobs.
The government has blamed recent attacks on Hutu extremists targeting minority Tutsis and those who witnessed the genocide to stop them giving evidence in trials of genocide suspects.

The people in the area identified the victims as members of the Kabeza and Neza families who left a squalid refugee camp in Tanzania in December and returned to their homes among banana plantations on a hilltop near Kibungo, 100 km (60 miles) east of Rwanda's capital Kigali.
Neighbours said police came to investigate the killings. But local authorities were not immediately available for comment.
